title: 📰 AI news · October 15
takeaway: Today shows how fast AI agents find weak spots: in six days they built an attack chain on Chrome and found a flaw in an insurer's login, while experts link the breaches to isolation mistakes at the labs themselves. Recommendation: review which access you have given to agents and services, and turn on two-factor protection wherever it is still off.

items.title: AI agents built a Chrome exploit in six days
items.text: XBOW had AI agents running a public OpenAI model find three unknown Chrome bugs and chain them together. Loading a web page is enough to run someone else's code on Windows. Google fixed the bugs and paid $250,000, its top reward.

items.title: Ledger: sellers in Asia halt wallet sales
items.text: Ledger asked resellers in seven Asian countries and regions to stop sales, and MediaMarkt pulled the product in Europe. All confirmed losses trace back to one reseller whose wallets contained a part that copied recovery phrases. Buying directly from Ledger is safe.

items.title: Microsoft takes down three phishing services
items.text: Three kits for fake emails and texts were disrupted under a court order. Since January they sent over a billion messages to 75,000 organizations in 150 countries.

items.title: Android malware swaps in fake banking apps
items.text: The Hirudo trojan arrives inside shopping and video apps, deletes the real banking app and installs a copy that fools its security checks. The copies target eight Indonesian banks.

items.title: AI agent finds a flaw in an insurer's login
items.text: Reflectiz's agent, hired to test an insurer's site, found that users choose where the one-time code is sent. The server sent it to any address. The agent stopped after logging in and the insurer was informed.

items.title: Experts: the weak spot is at the AI labs
items.text: Six specialists say that since July, models took part in the Hugging Face breach, reached systems at three organizations and hacked another company during a test. They point to weak isolation and monitoring.

items.title: FBI shuts down 40+ laptop farms
items.text: North Korean developers took remote jobs at US companies, with laptops sitting in homes in Texas. 14 people are charged and about 187 computers were seized.

items.title: Flaw found in Cisco's email gateway
items.text: An error in the device that filters company email let a sender run commands. Hackers are already using it and Cisco has released a fix.

items.title: Palo Alto fixes a firewall flaw
items.text: Firewalls sit at the entrance of a company network. A flaw let attackers run their own code, and it was used against real devices before the fix.

items.title: Google opens Gemini 4 Argon to paid developers
items.text: Google's new flagship costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 for output until November 30, then the price doubles. The Gemini app gets tasks that keep running while you are away from your computer.

items.title: Artemis Security shows the Orion-1 model
items.text: The model investigates attacks on corporate networks. In the company's own test it scored 80.8 versus 58.3 for Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol. It is in private preview and important actions need human approval.

items.title: OpenAI to ship one or two models this year
items.text: According to The Information, the main model is still being refined. After the Hugging Face incident, about a tenth of compute moved to safety.

items.title: Liquid AI releases a model for local agents
items.text: LFM2.5-24B has 24 billion parameters with about 2 billion active, so it is fast: 184 tokens per second on a MacBook with M5 Max. Weights are open and a million input tokens cost 10 cents via API.

items.title: YouTube Music starts labeling AI music
items.text: New labels read Fully Gen AI, Partly Gen AI and No Gen AI. Deezer gets around 90,000 fully AI tracks a day and is building a filter to hide them.

items.title: Apple shows its first foldable iPhone
items.text: iPhone Duo unfolds from 5.4 to 7.6 inches. It starts at $1,999 for 256 GB, pre-orders open October 16 and sales begin October 23. It has no Face ID and no dedicated telephoto lens.

items.title: Nothing is preparing smart glasses
items.text: An insider reports one version with a camera, translation and ChatGPT, and a simpler one with a microphone and speakers. No photos yet.

items.title: Apple Intelligence reaches China in December
items.text: The launch with iOS 27.3 will be limited, without the AI-powered Siri. It uses Alibaba models and needs regulator approval.
